newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-LATE STRIKE BY MCGRATH CHECKS ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LATE STRIKE BY MCGRATH CHECKS ENGLAND.

text.p: A late strike by Glenn McGrath prevented England seizing the initiative on the first day of the fourth test against Australia at Headingley on Thursday.

In his penultimate over of the day, paceman McGrath had Nasser Hussain snapped up by his captain Mark Taylor at first slip to leave England on 106 for three at the end of a rain-hit opening day in which only 36 overs were bowled.
England were put in to bat after Taylor won the toss for the fourth time in the series and Paul Reiffel in particular found plenty of life in a pitch that had become the subject of controversy.
A late switch in the pitch to be used brought suggestions the change had been made at the behest of David Graveney, chairman of the England selectors.

Australian tour manager Alan Crompton lodged an official complaint over the affair but later accepted assurances from the England and Wales Cricket Board that the decision had not been influenced by Graveney.

Rain permitted less than five full overs to be bowled until after the tea interval. Then Greg Blewett held a blinding catch to dismiss Mark Butcher for 24 and a straighforward one to send back Alec Stewart for seven after a poor shot.
Encouragingly for England, captain Michael Atherton was still there at close, having made a patient 34 in the 169 minutes of play possible.
England coach David Lloyd said:"Losing that last wicket has left things even. It was an intriguing battle. Now we've got to put some runs on the board."
Further rain was forecast for the second day on Friday, but the outlook was better for the remaining three days.
